newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia bonds find limited interest, ponder FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Australia bonds find limited interest, ponder FOMC.

text.p: *Australian bond yields succummbed to a typically quiet session ahead of Tuesday's FOMC meeting, and in front of two sets of key local wages data later this week.
*Spread little changed to U.S. after last week's tightening.
Australian bond yields succumbed to a typically quiet session ahead of Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting where the policy outlook still remains clouded, analysts said.

Although the risk of a tightening by the Fed has lessened in recently due to the data flow, a further pre-emptive tightening can not be ruled out, and even if they pass on policy this time round, they will still be seen as having a tightening bias.
"If the FOMC does raise rates it is likely that the long end will sell off to defend the differential," said Glenn Maguire, economist at Societe Generale.

Maguire also felt that a 25 basis point hike in the Fed Funds rate to 5.75 percent would make a local easing in official 6.0 percent interest rates unlikely as it would seriously threaten the Australian dollar by reducing international demand for local currency assets.

Talk of a possible easing by the Reserve Bank filtered through the markets last week when RBA governor Ian Macfarlane said the central bank was willing to let the economy grow faster, although he was still concerned about wages growth.
Final first quarter wages data and the government's latest report on enterprise bargaining agreements is due this week.

"While we believe that the promising growth outlook combined with upside risk to wages suggest that rates should remain on hold, if the RBA believes that growth can nudge up a bit more, then another rate cut remains on the agenda," said Su-Lin Ong, fixed income economist at Hambros Australia.

However, HSBC markets said in its monthly wages report that while there was little evidence to confirm an acceleration in wages, there was enough to throw doubt on the probability of a rate cut. There analysis showed that enterprise bargaining agreements has probably picked up slightly in the March quarter to around 4.65 percent, and higher than the December quarter.

The local market showed a mild underperformance against the U.S., where yields rose on Friday amid FOMC uncertainty and after stronger than expected housing starts data. Spreads also widened slightly to Canada based on levels during Friday's shortened session there ahead of today's Victoria Day holiday.
